title: SIEM export, backfill & failure runbook for audit/evidence logs
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook documents the operational design and implementation notes for storing, retaining, exporting, and re-ingesting Redwood audit and evidence logs to downstream SIEMs and cold storage. It focuses on: index layout, retention tiers, backfill strategy for missed exports, failure modes and mitigation, legal hold behavior, and automation hooks used by RBAC v2 and evidence automation subsystems.

Audience:
Security engineers, infra engineers, on-call SREs, compliance owners, and solutions engineers responsible for customer evidence requests and SIEM integrations.

Summary of goals:
- Ensure audit events are retained and queryable for SLO-aligned windows (hot store) and for legal/compliance windows (cold store).
- Provide reliable, idempotent SIEM export with guaranteed at-least-once delivery and dedup strategies for consumers.
- Define backfill and reindex paths for outages/out-of-order ingestion.
- Define automated detection and remediation for common failure modes with playbook steps.

High-level architecture:
- Ingress: application services (API, console, private deployments) push audit events into the Eventing tier (Kafka topic: audit.events.v2). Events conform to the audit-log schema (versioning via "schema_version" field).
- Processing: audit-pipeline consumers validate, enrich (RBAC v2 metadata, principal aliases), canonicalize timestamps, and write to hot-index (Elasticsearch cluster "audit-hot") and to a persistent object store (S3: s3://redwood-audit-evidence/raw/YYYY/MM/DD/).
- Export: export-worker reads from the hot-index (and S3 for older windows) and ships batched bundles to configured SIEM endpoints (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs Intake, customer S3/EFK). Exports are tracked in export-tracker DB (Postgres table audit_exports).
- Retention lifecycle: hot-index TTL = configurable (default 90 days). After TTL, indices are snapshot to cold S3 (parquet + index) and removed from hot. Cold storage retention default = 7 years (per compliance).

Indexing and index layout:
- Hot indices are time-based: audit-hot-YYYY.MM (monthly) for scale and snapshot efficiency. For high-volume customers we support per-customer sharded indices (audit-cust-<id>-YYYY.MM).
- Each document stored in hot index includes: event_id (UUID), occurred_at (RFC3339), ingested_at, schema_version, tenant_id, service, resource, action, outcome, principal {id,type,display_name,rbac_role_id}, request_payload_hash, metadata (list of tags).
- Primary query keys: event_id, tenant_id, occurred_at range, principal.id. Index mappings use keyword fields for aggregations and text fields for full-text where necessary.
- Indexed TTL and ILM policy: rollover when index size > 50GB or 30d and delete after hot TTL. Snapshots created before delete to cold bucket.

Retention policy (default):
- Hot (searchable): 90 days (configurable per plan).
- Warm/cold (searchable via archive job, higher latency): 1 year incremental snapshots kept on S3 with lightweight indices for date ranges 90d-1yr.
- Deep archive (nearline): 7 years persisted as parquet + manifest, accessible via rehydration job (longer latency, for legal/evidence requests).
- Delete: only after retention period and no active legal hold. Deletion is gated by compliance API.

Legal hold and evidence automation:
- Legal holds are annotated in the export-tracker and retention service with hold_id and expiration. Objects/indices with active holds are excluded from scheduled deletion and snapshot-to-delete flows.
- Evidence automation: evidence-collector service creates an evidence bundle manifest (list of event_ids + S3 paths + index refs), signs it, and stores it in s3://redwood-evidence-bundles/<case-id>/. A parallel entry is created in evidence_catalog DB.

SIEM export pipeline notes:
- Export worker reads from a durable cursor (offsets in export-tracker) which points at either hot index scroll cursor or S3 object ranges for older events.
- Exports are batched by tenant and destination to preserve ordering where required by customer contracts. Batch size and flush interval are tunable (default 5k events or 15s).
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once. Each batch tagged with batch_id and sequence_range. Consumers must handle idempotency (events have stable event_id). For Splunk, HEC dedup window is leveraged; for S3 exports we use manifest files and atomic commit keys.

Backfill strategy (missed window recovery):
1) Detection: monitoring alerts if export-tracker shows a gap > configured threshold (default 5m for streaming exports, 1h for batch).
2) Kickoff: backfill-controller schedules backfill job(s) segmented by time ranges and tenant (parallelism controlled by concurrency quota).
3) Source: backfill reads raw S3 archived files first (if beyond hot retention) otherwise uses hot index. It streams events through the same validation/enrichment pipeline to ensure consistent normalization.
4) Ordering and deduplication: backfill batches include original event_id and source_ingest_seq; export-worker uses these for idempotent writes. We maintain a per-destination ingest_history (recent batch_id hashes) to detect duplicates during replays.
5) Completion: backfill job writes a completion entry to export-tracker with backfill_job_id, time range, and checksum manifest.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Failure: schema drift (producer changed schema_version without migration).
  - Detect: pipeline validator rejects events (metric: validator.rejects).
  - Mitigation: route rejects to schema-dlq (S3 prefix s3://redwood-audit-dlq/schema/<date>/) and notify owner; attempt auto-adapt for additive compatible fields; product owner required to approve breaking changes.

- Failure: partial write to hot index (cluster shard fail) leading to gaps and inconsistent search results.
  - Detect: missing sequence gaps per tenant (monitoring playbook), write errors from ES client.
  - Mitigation: pipeline retries with exponential backoff; if still failing, mark batch as "pending-write" and store bundle in raw S3 for later reindex. Pager escalation if > 1h delayed for high-severity tenants.

- Failure: export delivery failures to SIEM endpoint (network, auth).
  - Detect: export-worker non-2xx responses, increase in DLQ rate.
  - Mitigation: retry with exponential backoff and jitter; switch to alternate endpoint (if configured) per routing policy; escalate to on-call after N retries (configurable, default 5). For long outages, store pending bundles in s3://redwood-export-pending/ with metadata so that downstream on-call can re-run exports manually.

- Failure: duplicate delivery (at-least-once semantics triggering duplicates in SIEM).
  - Detect: downstream duplicate metrics, or SIEM dedup complaints.
  - Mitigation: ensure each event contains idempotency keys (event_id + sequence_range). Provide customers with recommended dedup strategy (ingest-time idempotency by event_id). For internal replays, export-worker tags "replay=true" in metadata so SIEM parsers can skip if seen.

- Failure: long-lived backfill jobs causing resource exhaustion.
  - Detect: elevated CPU/IO on backfill nodes, queue length growth.
  - Mitigation: apply tenant throttles, progressive checkpointing (persist progress every N minutes), and autoscale backfill fleet with enforced upper bound. Stop lower-priority backfills in favor of emergency/legal hold jobs.

Operational runbook (common incidents):
1) Missing exports detected for tenant X (monitoring alert: export-gap > 1h).
   - Triage: confirm export-tracker offsets, check export-worker logs for last processed batch_id.
   - Remediate: if export-worker stalled, restart service; if downstream auth failed, rotate credentials and retry; if upstream ingress gap, open infra ticket and trigger re-ingest from raw S3.
   - Backfill: run backfill-controller for detected time range with concurrency=2 and tenant-level rate limit.
   - Postmortem: tag incident with root-cause and recovery steps.

2) Schema rejects > threshold
   - Triage: inspect representative records in schema-dlq. Identify schema_version change and producer.
   - Mitigate: if additive change, update parser to accept new fields; if breaking, revert producer or add translator shim.

3) Hot index write errors
   - Triage: check ES cluster health, shard allocation, and slowlogs.
   - Mitigate: if cluster degraded, scale ES nodes (hot), divert writes to raw S3 for eventual reindex. Execute reindex job once cluster healthy.

Monitoring and alerts (recommended):
- export-gap (per-tenant) > threshold -> P1 for enterprise tenants, P2 for self-serve.
- schema-reject-rate > baseline -> P1 if > 1% of traffic for > 15m.
- export-worker-error-rate increased (5xx) -> P1.
- unreadable S3 object errors -> P2 with auto-retry.
- backfill-job-failure -> P1 for legal hold jobs, P2 otherwise.

Instrumentation and observability notes:
- All pipeline steps must emit trace/span ids for distributed tracing. Use consistent tags: tenant_id, batch_id, batch_size, src (hot|cold), destination.
- Export-tracker provides an historical timeline UI (Console) for compliance teams to see exported ranges and job statuses.

Implementation notes and TODOs (engineering handoff):
- Add manifest-level checksums (parquet + JSON manifest) to all snapshots to speed verification during rehydration.
- Implement per-tenant retention overrides and a retention-change audit trail (reason, owner, timestamp).
- Support configurable deduplication TTL at export time to complement event_id-based dedup.
- Run tabletop exercise: simulate a 12h SIEM outage and exercise full re-ingest/backfill and post-export verification with compliance.

Appendix: quick CLI recovery commands (examples)
- Find export gap: SELECT * FROM audit_exports WHERE tenant_id='T123' ORDER BY last_exported_at DESC LIMIT 10;
- Trigger backfill (admin): backfill-controller --tenant=T123 --start=2024-10-01T00:00Z --end=2024-10-02T00:00Z --concurrency=2
- Reindex from S3: reindex-tool --src=s3://redwood-audit-evidence/raw/2024/10/01/ --target=elastic://audit-hot-2024.10 --batch=5000

Notes and known constraints:
- Due to multi-tenant performance characteristics, backfills for large tenants (>10M events/day) require manual coordination with infra to provision temporary index capacity.
- Legal hold overrides ingestion retention and must be applied before scheduled deletes; currently legal hold propagation can take up to 5 minutes.

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: Priya Nair (security infra)
- Secondary: Marcus Li (platform SRE)
- Pager: #sec-oncall (follow escalation in handbook)

Contacts and references:
- Evidence retention playbook (linked artifact)
- RBAC v2 design doc (confluence:RBAC-V2-2024)
- Export worker implementation: github:infra/audit-pipeline

End of runbook.

Unresolved questions / open actions:
- Confirm per-tier retention SLAs for Dedicated customers (product to finalize policy).
- Decide whether replay metadata should be omitted by default when exporting to customer-managed S3 (privacy discussion).
- Add automated manifest verification post-export (ticketed).
